What to do when a source has no page number (APA citations)
My source doesn't have page numbers, how do I cite it?
How do I cite a website or eBook without page numbers in APA?
Torrens requires page numbers for all in-text citations. When a page number isn't available, use one of these instead:

- **Paragraph number** — (Author surname, year, para. x), e.g. (Smith, 2025, para. 3)
- **Chapter/section title + paragraph number** — (Author surname, year, section title, para. x), e.g. (Smith, 2020, an overview of nursing practice, para. 2)
- **Page range from an eBook reader** — (Author surname, year, pp. x–y), e.g. (Smith, 2020, pp. 1–5)

chunks.title: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?
chunks.text:
What is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?
What counts as AI?
Is the predictive text on my phone considered AI?
AI refers to computer systems that perform tasks normally involving human judgement, pattern recognition, or language understanding — by analysing data to find patterns, not through true understanding. That means AI output can sometimes be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or misleading.

Everyday examples already embedded in digital tools:

- Your phone suggesting the next word while typing
- Search engines predicting what you're looking for
- Study tools generating summaries
- Research databases recommending related articles
- Writing tools suggesting grammar or clarity improvements

At university, AI tools should support your learning and thinking, not replace them — human judgement and critical review remain essential.

What is Generative AI (GenAI)?
What's the difference between AI and generative AI?
What can generative AI tools actually create?
Generative AI (GenAI) creates new content by identifying and predicting patterns in existing data, in response to a user prompt — unlike AI systems that just analyse or classify information.

GenAI can generate:

- Text
- Images
- Audio and music
- Video
- Computer code

Example uses: brainstorming/summarising/writing help, generating images from descriptions, creating audio/music/video, and assisting with coding.

chunks.title: How to use AND/OR/NOT (Boolean operators) in a database search
chunks.text:
How to use AND/OR/NOT (Boolean operators) in a database search
What are Boolean operators and how do I use them?
How do I combine keywords in a database search?
Use AND, OR, and NOT to connect search terms and broaden or narrow results:

- **AND** — each result contains **all** search terms
- **OR** — each result contains **at least one** search term
- **NOT** — results **do not contain** the specified terms

**Example:** (Ethics OR social implications OR controversy OR unethical OR intellectual property) AND (generative AI OR artificial intelligence OR AI art OR computer generated art)

[Watch the video on Boolean operators](https://library.torrens.edu.au/howtovideos/boolean) for more detail.

chunks.title: What is the CRAP test for evaluating a source?
chunks.text:
What is the CRAP test for evaluating a source?
What is the CRAP test?
How do I check if a source is credible enough to use?
The CRAP test checks a source's credibility across four areas:

- **Currency** — How recent is it? When was it published/last updated? If older, is it based on established knowledge?
- **Reliability** — Does it seem balanced, and is it backed by research, evidence, and references? Is it [peer-reviewed](https://library.torrens.edu.au/howtovideos/peerreview)?
- **Authority** — Are the author and publisher qualified and expert in the subject area?
- **Purpose/point of view** — What's the intent? Is there bias? Is it relevant to your purpose?

If you're unsure about a source, ask your Learning Facilitator or [contact the library via Chat](http://faq.torrens.edu.au/chat/widget/9191db96e76bee9bc5f41bb9b313bfff).

How do I get a copy of my academic transcript?
How long does it take to get my completion letter or testamur?
How much does it cost to request an academic document?
Available documents depend on your enrolment type:

- **Higher Education:** Official Academic Transcript*, Completion Letter, Testamur**
- **Vocational Education & Training:** Official Statement of Attainment*, Completion Letter, Testamur**

\* Only available once grades are published after your first study period.
\*\* Only released once you've provided your USI and all fees are cleared.

**How to request:**
1. Go to the [Academic Document Request Portal](https://academicdocumentrequest.torrens.edu.au/) (single sign-on, or enter your details directly)
2. Select the document type and quantity
3. Choose your delivery method
4. Confirm and pay — **fees are non-refundable**, so check your details before submitting

- Hard copy: minimum 10 working days for processing and postage
- Documents from before 2016: minimum 6-8 weeks
- Replacement testamur (lost/stolen/damaged): you may need to provide a [statutory declaration](https://www.ag.gov.au/legal-system/statutory-declarations)

chunks.text:
How to request an assessment extension, by length of extension
How do I ask for an extension on an assignment?
Do I need documentation to get an extension?
How many days before the deadline do I need to apply for an extension?
Before requesting, note that extensions can delay feedback, future assessments, and sometimes progression to later subjects.

- **1 to 7 calendar days** — no supporting documentation needed, but you must give a detailed explanation. Submit via the "Assignments" section on MyLearn, at least 3 calendar days before the due date (unless the delay was unavoidable).
- **8 to 14 calendar days** — documentation required. Same MyLearn submission process and 3-day notice.
- **Over 14 calendar days** — use the Assessment Special Consideration Form ([Torrens University](https://torrens.blackboard.com/bbcswebdav/xid-4652143_1) | [Think Education](https://torrens.blackboard.com/bbcswebdav/xid-2796802_1)) and submit it with supporting documents to your Learning Facilitator. This form also covers WIL placement deferral and other modified assessment arrangements.

If you're not on MyLearn, submit your request directly to your Learning Facilitator(s).

If you need extra support, [Study Support](https://studenthub.torrens.edu.au/Hub/Study-Support) and the [Counselling service](https://studenthub.torrens.edu.au/Hub/Support/Counselling) are available.

The SRC works to make student community better, through three pillars:

- **Community** — creating a welcoming, diverse, inclusive campus; running events and workshops for students to network and connect

chunks.title: What are my obligations as an international student (visa, OSHC, study load)?

How much of my course can I study online as an international student?
What do I need to maintain as an international student visa holder?
Do I need a USI (Unique Student Identifier) to graduate?
Under the ESOS (Education Services for Overseas Students) Framework, international students on an Australian student visa, studying onshore, must:

- Maintain a valid CoE and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the duration of study
- Advise the University of passport details and any visa status changes
- Enrol in **no more than one-third (33%)** of their course online — above that, you need to take on-campus classes
- Enrol in at least one face-to-face subject during a compulsory study period
- Complete the course within the duration stated in their CoE
- Enrol full-time, unless approved for a reduced study load, leave of absence, or compassionate/compelling circumstances
- Abide by their student visa conditions

See [Equivalent Full-Time Student Load (EFTSL) information](https://www.torrens.edu.au/how-to-apply/fees-scholarships/tuition-fees#EFTSL) for more detail.

Separately: if you're completing any study in Australia, you must have a Unique Student Identifier (USI), or you may not be eligible to graduate.

- Are enrolled in a fee-paying place at a FEE-HELP provider
- Are enrolled in an eligible course by the census date
- Submit the Request for FEE-HELP loan form to your provider by the census date
- Have an available HELP balance
- Have a Unique Student Identifier (USI) before your first census date (for enrolments from 1 January 2021)

More detail: [Study Assist — FEE-HELP](https://www.studyassist.gov.au/help-loans/fee-help)

- **Loan limit (2026 census dates):** $129,883 for most students; $186,544 for approved medicine, dentistry, veterinary science, and certain aviation courses. Indexation doesn't count toward your limit.
- **Loan fee:** a 20% FEE-HELP loan fee applies to some undergraduate study, but **not** if your census date is on/after 1 January 2019 and you're at a Table B provider like Torrens.
- **Repayment:** starts via the tax system once you earn above the compulsory repayment threshold ($67,000 for the 2025-2026 income year).
